extracted.intended_audience: members of the American Mathematical Society (AMS) eligible to vote / AMS membership
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and submission guidelines for the AMS 1992 election: mailing schedule and deadlines for ballots, replacement-ballot process and required statements, how to submit nominations, and limits/verification for candidate biographical material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ballot mailing schedule and receipt deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: The ballots for election of members of the Council and Board of Trustees of the Society for 1993 will be mailed on or shortly after September 10, in order for members to receive their ballots well in advance of the November 10 deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ballots mailed ~Sept 10; deadline for receipt of ballots is November 10. Although replacement ballots will be supplied on request, the deadline for receipt of ballots will not be extended to accommodate these special cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement ballot eligibility and request timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A member who has not received a ballot by October 10, 1992, or who has received a ballot but has accidentally spoiled it, may write after that date to the Secretary of the AMS requesting a second ballot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request should include the individual's member code and the address to which the replacement ballot should be sent. Address: Secretary of the AMS, Post Office Box 6248, Providence, RI 02940. Upon receipt of the request, a second ballot will be sent by first class or air mail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement ballot return requirements and attestation
rubrics_metrics.description: The second ballot will be indistinguishable from the original and must be returned in an inner envelope supplied with it, on the outside of which is a statement to be signed by the member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The required signed statement text: "The ballot in this envelope is the only ballot that I am submitting in this election. I understand that if this statement is not correct then no ballot of mine will be counted." Failure to meet these return requirements may invalidate the replacement ballot; note deadline is not extended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Members urged to consult AMS Bylaws before voting
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to casting their ballots members are urged to consult the following articles and sections of the Bylaws of the Society: article I, section 1; article II, sections 1, 2; article III, sections 1, 2, 3; article IV, sections 1, 2, 4; article VII, sections 1, 2, 5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The complete text of the Bylaws appears on pages 1177-1182 of the November 1991 issue of the Notices. Members are advised to consult these sections to inform their votes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggestions for nominations — submission process and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Each year members are given the opportunity to propose names of individuals they deem qualified for nomination. Candidates will be nominated by the Council to fill positions whose terms expire January 31, 1994.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members are requested to write their suggestions in the appropriate spaces on the form and send the completed form to AMS Nominating Committee, Post Office Box 6248, Providence, RI 02940, to arrive no later than November 10, 1992. Positions to suggest are listed (President-Elect, Vice-President, Members-at-large of the Council (5), Member of the Board of Trustees (1), etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate biographical submission limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Biographical information about the candidates has been verified by the candidates. A candidate had the opportunity to make a statement of not more than 200 words on any subject matter without restriction and to list up to five of her or his research papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biographical statements were limited to 200 words and up to five research papers could be listed; these constraints governed the material included in the Notices to assist members in voting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation for petition-nominated candidates
rubrics_metrics.description: An (*) indicates the individual was nominated in response to a petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidate lists in the Notices mark petition-only nominees with an asterisk so voters can identify petition-nominated individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of election materials in the Notices to increase turnout
rubrics_metrics.description: In an effort to increase the number of ballots returned in the election process, the Society has decided to include in the Notices all the pertinent election material, including biographies and statements of the candidates in the upcoming election.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This inclusion is intended to assist members in filling out the ballots that will be mailed, and the officers encourage members to return ballots. The Secretary urges members to study the printed material and to return a completed ballot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problems causing nonreceipt of ballots and recommended remedy
rubrics_metrics.description: There has been a recurring problem concerning members who state they have not received ballots; reasons include failure of local delivery systems, failure to notify Providence office of address changes, postal service failures, and human errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To alleviate the problem, the replacement ballot procedure is available (see replacement ballot eligibility). Members who have not received ballots by October 10 should request a second ballot as specified; include member code and address in the request.
